# R0 first births are generated by within-component contact-address differences

For a rank-zero occupied prefix, the new site's homology image is exactly
the integer span of **contact lift-address differences within each old
occupied component**. This turns the fork's boolean first-birth flag into a
direction-bearing local attachment mechanism. No new union-find algorithm
is proposed; the result interprets the existing displacement data.

## Exact convention and theorem

The current NN graph is `Z^2 / P Z^2`, with columns of P the physical period
vectors. An oriented nearest-neighbor edge has a lifted unit step
`delta in {(+/-1,0),(0,+/-1)}`. The production backend converts a closed
physical displacement w to period coordinates by `P^{-1}w`, implemented
exactly as `adj(P)*w/det(P)`.

Let O have ambient homology image rank zero and let v be vacant. Since
`H1(torus;Z)=Z^2` is torsion-free, every cycle in each occupied component C
has exactly zero lifted displacement. Thus choose a potential p_C(u) equal
to the displacement of any old path from a root of C to u; it is path
independent even if C contains contractible cycles.

For each incident edge e from v to an occupied u in C define

\[
 \alpha_e=\delta_e-p_C(u).
\]

Choose one contact e_C as an anchor for each touched component. Then

\[
 \boxed{\operatorname{im}H_1(O\cup\{v\}\to\mathbb T^2)
 =\left\langle P^{-1}(\alpha_e-\alpha_{e_C}):
       e\text{ contacts }C,\ e\ne e_C\right\rangle_{\mathbb Z}.}
\]

Every difference lies in the period lattice, so its period coordinates are
integers. Changing the old component root translates all its alpha values
by one constant and leaves these differences unchanged. Absolute alpha
values in different components cannot be subtracted to manufacture a
cycle: their gauges are independent and no old path joins them.

**Proof.** Choose a spanning tree in every old occupied component and attach
each touched tree to v using its anchor contact. These edges form a spanning
tree of the new merged component. Its non-tree old edges have zero gain by
the R0 premise. Every remaining contact e closes a fundamental cycle
`v -> u_e -> old tree -> u_anchor -> v`, with displacement
`delta_e-p_C(u_e)+p_C(u_anchor)-delta_anchor=alpha_e-alpha_anchor`.
Fundamental cycles form an integer basis of the graph cycle group. Their
images therefore generate the entire new homology image, not merely a
selected set of sufficient witnesses. Untouched old components still have
zero image. This proves equality.

This is exactly the physical convention of the existing backend at
`84018e19:src/threshold_rank_integer_period_mc.cpp`: `find()` returns the
root-to-vertex potential; `one_step_completion()` stores
`root_position=step-found.displacement`; and its within-root differences
are converted by `quotient.winding()`. The existing routine applies a
transverse test in R1. The theorem specifies the full two-dimensional
generator meaning when the old rank is zero.

## The three singleton outcomes

Let L_v be the subgroup in the box and take its rank over Q.

- rank0: no first homological birth, even if the insertion creates graph
  cycles or joins several components.
- rank1: ordinary first birth, with primitive winding direction given by
  any nonzero generator. Integer multiplicities are retained by L_v rather
  than inferred from the primitive direction alone.
- rank2: a direct `R0 -> R2` event; the same insertion causes both K1 and K2.

For a nondegenerate NN site there are at most four contact edges. The rank2
case consequently has a small exhaustive structural distinction:

1. One old component's contacts supply two independent address differences.
   It needs at least three contacts; one extra contact may be present.
2. No individual old component supplies rank2, but two components supply
   non-collinear rank1 images. Each needs at least two contacts, so the
   only possible contact multiplicities are **2+2**.

Indeed, if touched component C has m_C contacts, at most m_C-1 new cycle
generators come from it. A rank-one line from two components can be the
same line, in which case their union still has rank1. Counting contacts
or components alone does not decide any of these ambient-rank outcomes.
The contact cyclic ports and winding differences identify the attachment;
no macroscopic arm count or exponent follows from this finite statement.

## Three paper configurations on the nondegenerate 5-by-5 square torus

Take `P=5I`, v=(0,0), and interpret all coordinates modulo5. Each path below
lists **all** occupied sites in that example; all other sites are vacant.
They are explicit paper configurations, not additional N325/N425 samples.

**Same component, three contacts, no homological birth.** Occupy the path

```
(4,0)--(4,1)--(0,1)--(1,1)--(1,0).
```

It is an induced tree. The new v contacts W=(4,0), N=(0,1), E=(1,0).
With E as root, all three alpha addresses are `(1,0)`. Adding v creates
two contractible graph cycles but all winding generators are zero.

**Same component, three contacts, direct rank2 theta birth.** Instead occupy

```
(4,0)--(3,0)--(2,0)--(1,0)--(1,4)--(1,3)--(0,3)--(0,2)--(0,1).
```

This is again an induced tree, with the same three contacts W,N,E and with
S=(0,4) still vacant. Set p(E)=0. The potentials are
`p(W)=(3,0)` and `p(N)=(-1,-4)`, using the actual lifted steps along the path.
Therefore

```
alpha_E=(1,0), alpha_W=(-4,0), alpha_N=(1,5),
P^(-1)(alpha_W-alpha_E)=(-1,0),
P^(-1)(alpha_N-alpha_E)=(0,1).
```

The two generators are independent. The added site and E are the two
branch points of a theta backbone. The change from the preceding example
is not the number or component partition of contacts; it is their lift
address difference.

**Two old components, two contacts each, direct rank2 figure-eight birth.**
Occupy the horizontal path `(1,0)--(2,0)--(3,0)--(4,0)` and the disjoint
vertical path `(0,1)--(0,2)--(0,3)--(0,4)`. Both are rank-zero components.
The new v closes a horizontal and a vertical cycle. With each positive
neighbor as its component anchor, their winding differences are `(-1,0)`
and `(0,-1)`. Each component supplies just one line; together they generate
rank2. The cycles meet at the inserted site.

## Degenerate quotients and the current production scope

The boxed formula assumes that adding v creates no self-loop at v. With a
degenerate quotient, add each such new loop's gain explicitly to the
generator list. Parallel edges must always remain distinct **edge contacts**:
two edges to the same occupied neighbor can have different lifted steps and
a nonzero difference. Deduplicating only by neighbor label can lose a birth.
The spanning-tree proof otherwise applies unchanged to the gain multigraph.

For the current HNF representatives `[[N,shear],[0,1]]`, the four NN neighbor
labels are `v+1,v-1,v-shear,v+shear mod N`. The declared N325 shears57/18 and
N425 shears132/268 give four distinct neighbors, none v. Thus neither new
self-loops nor parallel NN contacts occur in these four production
geometries. The illustrative5-by-5 torus has the same nondegeneracy. No
claim about a crossing NN+NNN matching graph or a white-arm lift is required.

## Why this is a new R0 mechanism readout, not the old R1 cut problem

In R1 there is already an essential line; completion asks whether added
connectivity creates a transverse winding, and the existing two-terminal
mapping exploits that pre-existing carrier. In R0 there is no such line
or two-boundary choice. One insertion can create either one or both
independent directions, as the explicit examples show. The vector contact
span is therefore the appropriate immediate-source mark, while a boolean
g01 or a contact count discards its mechanism.

The minimal future augmentation for a sampled next label would retain its
occupied-contact component partition, NN port/edge identities, within-root
relative winding addresses and generated rank/direction. It need not invent
another connectivity engine. This note does not alter or restart the running
fork production; acquisition of those marks remains a later decision.

Scientific card: exact finite contact-cycle generators separate no birth,
rank1 birth and the two origins of direct rank2 birth. They provide a
direction-bearing interpretation for R0-supported first-label information
in `84018e19`, while distinguishing it from the R1 two-terminal mechanism.
The proof uses the existing public gain convention and three paper examples,
not new MC, DP, retrospective source validation or an asymptotic arm theorem.
